title: Headroom smoothing, emergency fallback, and post-incident remediation for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Summary:
During a customer-facing run of Dedicated capacity (eu-west-1 pools) on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated shortfalls where pool throughput dropped below committed SLA for 12-minute windows. This ticket captures the incident summary, immediate mitigations, decisions made during response, and the resulting post-incident action items to prevent recurrence.

What happened (brief):
- Sudden increase in long-tail request latencies triggered autoscaler hysteresis to under-provision headroom for hot pools.
- A kernel-selection regression (deployed in runtime-1.19) increased per-instance memory pressure for medium-sequence workloads which reduced ALB healthy capacity.
- Autoscaler health signals (eviction count and runtime OOM proxy) were noisy; the predictive headroom estimator underestimated burst requirement for reserved pools.

Impact:
- Several customer Dedicated tenants experienced degraded throughput and elevated request queuing for 10-30 minutes. SLOs slipped for ~8 customers in eu-west-1 (payment/checkout flows impacted for two customers).

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Interplay between a kernel selection regression and an over-aggressive headroom estimator in the autoscaler caused the control loop to reduce spare capacity during a transient workload spike. The runtime regression amplified memory pressure leading to instance churn.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident: 
- Rolled back runtime-1.19 kernel selection change on eu-west-1 dedicated pool (hotfix deployed 2026-03-09 20:45 UTC). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8321
- Forced temporary headroom floor of +30% for all Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 for 2 hours to allow stabilization (console change: https://console.redwood.ai/#/admin/pools/eu-west-1/settings)
- Enabled conservative throttle policy for best-effort requests to preserve reserved capacity for SLA routes (route-level policy link: https://console.redwood.ai/#/routes/ratelimit)

steps_taken:
1) Stabilize: rollback runtime change, set headroom floor, enable conservative throttling for non-SLA traffic.
2) Forensic: collected flamegraphs and kernel memory metrics, exported autoscaler decision traces, and captured KV cache hit/miss rates for affected instances.
3) Short-term policy: added a cooldown override to prevent headroom estimator from scaling below 20% during detected spikes.
4) Communication: notified affected customers via status.redwood.ai incident CRIT-2026-03-09-DED and sent individual follow-ups to enterprise contacts.

Artifacts collected:
- Flamegraphs and mem profiles: https://storage.redwood.ai/incidents/ENG-59123/profiles.tar.gz
- Autoscaler decision trace: https://logs.redwood.ai/trace/eng-59123-autoscaler
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/fleet/throughput?orgId=1&var_pool=dedicated-eu-west
analysis_and_decisions:
Technical trade-offs considered: 
- Option A: widen static headroom (simple, immediate) vs Option B: redesign predictive headroom estimator (longer-term, more accurate). We applied a hybrid: a temporary static floor + blockers for immediate safety while owning a project to harden the estimator.
- Kernel selection rollback restores current performance but prevents per-model memory optimizations in the short term; we accepted the rollback to preserve customer SLAs and included a follow-up to re-evaluate kernel selection under controlled load tests.

Decisions made in post-incident review: 
- Ship autoscaler guardrails that include a minimum headroom floor, max-change-per-minute rate limit, and explicit OOM/eviction signal weighting.
- Add a per-pool canary path for runtime kernel selection that exercises a small percentage of capacity before global rollout.
- Improve telemetry of autoscaler decision inputs into an indexed trace store for fast RCA in future incidents.
acceptance_criteria:
- Autoscaler has headroom floor and rate-limit configuration flags deployed to staging and prod (can be toggled via console).
- New canary path for kernel-selection is implemented and validated in test cluster with <2% error during 72h soak.
- Runbook updated with clear run/rollback steps and playbook for forced headroom floors and throttles.
- Postmortem published with customer impact summary and timeline; customers contacted and compensation offers approved by PM when applicable.
